'''''Parodia magnifica''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Cactaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern Brazil. One of several species called '''ball cactus''', it is also called '''balloon cactus'''.<ref name=EofC/> It grows to {{convert|7|-|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad, with heavily ribbed, spherical to columnar, spiny and hairy stems, bearing pale yellow flowers in summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref> Its natural habitat is cool, dry temperate grassland at elevations of up to {{convert|800 |m|ft|abbr=on}}.<ref name=EofC>{{cite web 
| url = http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/CACTI/Family/Cactaceae/20453/Parodia_magnifica | title = ''Parodia magnifica'' 
| publisher = The Encyclopedia of Cacti | access-date = 18 April 2018}}</ref> Populations are sparse and fragmented, and it has been designated as "Endangered" by the [[IUCN Red List]].<ref name="iucn status 11 November 2021" />

In cultivation it must be kept above {{convert|10|C|F|abbr=on}}, so in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions is grown under glass. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Parodia magnifica''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/236185/Parodia-magnifica/Details | access-date = 16 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 72 
| publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 17 April 2018}}</ref> 

==Synonyms==
* ''Notocactus magnificus''<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.tropicos.org/Name/50180515?tab=synonyms | title = ''Parodia magnifica'' (synonyms) | publisher = Tropicos | access-date = 18 April 2018}}</ref> 
* ''Eriocactus magnificus''

The plant may still be found listed under these synonyms in the horticultural literature.
